Treatment summary
Patient presented following a rear-end motor vehicle collision with complaints of neck pain, stiffness, and headache
radiating into the upper shoulders. The reported mechanism of injury is consistent with the force and direction of the
impact, and the presenting symptoms are in keeping with a cervical strain pattern. No prior injury to the cervical spine
or upper back is known from the history obtained. Conservative management was provided over 28 visits, including
manual therapy, therapeutic exercise, and home stretching instructions. Care extended somewhat beyond the typical
course for this type of injury, with gradual improvement reported over time. Cervical range of motion, neurological
screening, and palpation findings were largely within normal limits at each assessment, and cervical imaging showed
no acute abnormality. Therefore, the clinical picture relies heavily on the patient's self-reported pain levels and
functional limitations. Billing records reviewed for this episode reflect single, non-duplicated chagres for each service
rendered.
</page>

Rate each feature below that THIS page gives evidence about. Leave out a feature the page
says nothing about. The ratings are listed from least to most suspicious.
- injury_crash_fit: Does the claimed injury fit the type and force of the crash? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- treatment_growth: Did the treatment grow beyond what this injury needs? Allowed: Normal, Elevated, Disproportionate, Extreme.
- objective_support: Do objective tests (imaging, exam findings) support the complaints? Allowed: Strong, Partial, Predominantly subjective, Contradicted.
- pre_existing_condition: Did an earlier condition of the same body area add to the complaints? Allowed: None, Minor, Material, Predominant.
- duplicate_billing: Was the same service, visit or part billed twice? Allowed: None, Possible, Confirmed.

  spelling errors as they are,
- "reason": one short sentence.
